description: How dependency versions move in the slafhas and Grundkoll repositories. Each repository's renovate.json extends this preset and adds its own groups: the couplings differ per stack (EF Core and Npgsql, tiptap, tailwind), and each was learned in its own repository, so each stays there with its reason.

This preset replaced Dependabot's version updates in those repositories, and its security updates for direct dependencies. It keeps what their dependabot.yml files did -- one round a week, Monday, Stockholm time; majors arrive as their own pull request unless a repository holds them back; GitHub Actions minors and patches in one pull request -- and adds one thing Dependabot could not do on GitHub's free plan: a security fix merges itself once every check is green.

It is not the 2Fivers preset. That one merges tooling by itself because `pnpm check` exercises every tool in full; nothing in these repositories proves tooling that way, so here only security fixes merge themselves.

Renovate works at night: the weekly round and every automerge happen between 02:00 and 06:00. updateNotScheduled is false, so an open branch is rebased only in that window. That is what Dependabot's `rebase-strategy: disabled` was for: a push to the base branch used to rebase every open dependency pull request and start a CI run for each, none of them about what was pushed. A branch that is wanted sooner is rebased by ticking its box in the pull request.
Merging deploys nothing. Only a published GitHub release deploys these repositories, so a merged update waits on the default branch for a release, made by a person or by the release bot.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate is the CVE channel for direct dependencies. It reads the repository's Dependabot alerts and the OSV database and opens a pull request outside the schedule, with the lockfile updated. TWO DAYS OLD FIRST, the same minimumReleaseAge as every other update. Renovate's own default for a vulnerability fix is no wait at all, and with it a version published together with an advisory that names it as the fix would merge that night and leave with the next release: the one path into a repository with nothing aging in front of it. The wait costs almost nothing, because a fixed version is nearly always older than that by the time its advisory arrives (homelab-docs ADR 0121). While the fix is younger, Renovate creates no branch (internalChecksFilter strict) and lists it under 'Pending Status Checks' on the Dependency Dashboard. Ticking it there opens the pull request at once, for a human to merge; automerge still waits for the age. AUTOMERGED once every check is green, inside automergeSchedule like every other automerge: Renovate skips `schedule` for a vulnerability fix but still checks automergeSchedule, so a fix that comes of age in the afternoon merges that night. The setting is forced over every packageRule, so a fix that is a major, or one a repository holds back, merges itself too; with vulnerabilityFixStrategy `lowest` that happens only when no minor or patch carries the fix. A human can still stop one by closing its pull request. Dependabot's own security updates stay on beside this, because Renovate does not fix a transitive dependency; their pull requests are merged by a human.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions minors and patches in one pull request, as every repository's dependabot.yml grouped them. Majors arrive on their own.
